question: Which of the following is NOT a type of paragraph formatting in MS-Word 365?
solution:
The correct answer is **Precise**

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**The formatting options available in the 'Paragraph' setting window in MS Word 2016 are:

 
• Spacing.
 
• Indentation.
 
• Pagination under the option Line and Page breaks.
 
• Alignment.

​Paragraph formatting options are described as:

 
• Alignment

 
 
• Alignment or justification refers to the way in which the lines of a paragraph are aligned.
 
• There are four types of alignment, namely, left, center, right, and justified.
 
 
 
• Indentation
 
 
• The value in the Before text box specifies the width of the additional empty space that is inserted between the margin and the text on the left-hand side of a paragraph of left-to-right text.
 
• The value in the After text box specifies the width of the additional empty space that is inserted between the text and the margin on the right-hand side of a paragraph of left-to-right text.
 
• A negative value specifies the distance by which the text extends beyond the respective margin.
 
 
 
• Spacing
 
 
• The spacing between two paragraphs is determined by the spacing before one paragraph and the spacing after the preceding paragraph, which are displayed and can be modified in the Before and After boxes.
 
• Line spacing refers to the vertical distance between the lines within a paragraph.
 
• It determines the location of each line relative to the line above it.
 
 
 
• Line and Page Breaks tab (Pagination)
 
 
• The paragraph formatting options on the Line and Page Breaks tab under pagination of the Paragraph dialog box can help you control where automatic page breaks occur in your document.
